business: Quilt: a phone app where an AI assistant builds and fills small life apps (budget, groceries, classes, to-dos, subscriptions) from a photo or a sentence
target: Full-time University of Utah undergrads, 18 to 24, managing their own money for the first time, phone-first
where: Salt Lake City, University of Utah campus; online (Android app and website)

segments.name: Mostly supported by family or aid

behaviours.name: App hopper
behaviours.how: Downloads a new app, uses it for a week, forgets it.

behaviours.name: Notes-app loyalist
behaviours.how: Keeps lists and money notes in the phone's Notes app and sees no reason to move.

behaviours.name: Free-tier only
behaviours.how: Never pays for an app; uses free versions and student deals.

behaviours.name: Organised planner
behaviours.how: Already uses a planner, Notion or a spreadsheet and likes control.

behaviours.name: Stressed and behind
behaviours.how: Has been hit by a late fee or a forgotten renewal this semester and wants it to stop.

behaviours.name: Reads every review
behaviours.how: Checks App Store or Play ratings and Reddit before trying anything.

behaviours.name: Loyal to a finance app
behaviours.how: Already uses YNAB, Cleo or Rocket Money with a bank linked.

objections: I already use my Notes app and it's free
Another subscription is the problem I'm trying to fix
Will the AI read my receipt right, or will I end up fixing it?
I won't keep it up after the first week
Who sees my spending and my photos?
Why not just use Notion, it's free for students
Credits sound like I'll run out at the wrong moment
habits: you shop at Smith's or a corner store near campus once or twice a week
you pay for Spotify and one or two other subscriptions you rarely think about
you check your bank app only when something feels wrong
you get syllabi as PDFs at the start of each semester
you lift at the campus gym a few times a week
you split takeout and groceries with roommates
